oewn-04650754-n.learner: a rough, sharp and bitter way of speaking or acting.
examples: She spoke with such bitterness that nobody dared to answer her.

connotation.why: sour, hostile manner set against plain sharpness or tartness

oewn-05725062-n.learner: the taste you get when something like strong coffee or quinine medicine is in your mouth.
examples: The bitterness of the black coffee made her face twist.

oewn-05002002-n.learner: the quality of having a harsh, unpleasant taste.
examples: The bitterness of these wild lemons makes them hard to eat.

oewn-07547101-n.learner: the feeling you have when you are pleased and satisfied with yourself.
examples: After the easy first win, his complacency showed in every move he made.

oewn-00607261-a.learner: fitting well with your comfort, your purpose, or your needs.
examples: Elizabeth saw what he was doing, and at the first convenient pause turned to him with an arch smile
It was rather small, but well built and convenient
The house was very convenient, with wide halls and many large rooms.

oewn-02648898-v.learner: to put something off until a later time.
examples: and till the morrow their going was deferred.
perhaps I may defer it till Kitty runs away.

oewn-00879879-v.learner: to give way to what someone else wants or thinks.
examples: On questions of law, she always deferred to her older brother.

connotation.why: yielding framed as respect, set against give in or submit

oewn-07518219-n.learner: a feeling of having no respect for someone or something, together with a strong dislike.
examples: said Elizabeth, colouring with astonishment and disdain
with an expression of civil disdain, thus accosted her

connotation.why: set against contempt, scorn and plain dislike

oewn-06732153-n.learner: something said or written to a person that shows no respect for them by talking down to them.
examples: His letter was polite disdain from start to finish, explaining simple things to her as if to a child.

oewn-04900982-n.learner: being careful not to spend more money or use more things than you need.
examples: Mrs. Bennet had no turn for economy
When first Mr. Bennet had married, economy was held to be perfectly useless

connotation.why: careful spending set against thrift, stinginess and meanness

oewn-08383680-n.learner: the whole system by which goods are made, shared out, and used.
examples: The country's economy grew quickly after the war.

oewn-05652572-n.learner: using what you have well, without waste.
examples: The old dancer moved with great economy, never wasting a step.

oewn-00193462-n.learner: something done to save money; a cut in what something costs.
examples: Walking to work every day was one small economy she made.

oewn-00513958-v.learner: to make someone or something able to do a task.
examples: Nothing but concern for Elizabeth could enable Bingley to keep his countenance.
these four evenings have enabled them to ascertain that they both like Vingt-un better than Commerce

oewn-01273978-s.learner: done very fast and without enough careful thought.
examples: I would wish not to be hasty in censuring anyone
It was a hasty decision, and she soon regretted it.

connotation.why: speed blamed as thoughtless, set against quick

examples: Elizabeth jumped out; and after giving each of them a hasty kiss, hurried into the vestibule

connotation.why: too quick, set against quick or brief

oewn-05775730-n.learner: the power of your mind to make pictures of things or events.
examples: Lakes, mountains, and rivers, shall not be jumbled together in our imaginations

oewn-05633248-n.learner: making a picture in your mind of something that is not real and not there for your senses.
examples: indulge your imagination in every possible flight which the subject will afford
In Lydia's imagination, a visit to Brighton comprised every possibility of earthly happiness.

oewn-05641705-n.learner: the ability to find clever ways to deal with problems that are not usual.
examples: Mending the boat with only a rope and an old shoe took real imagination.

oewn-02588345-s.learner: caring most about money and the things it can buy.
examples: I should be sorry to think our friend mercenary.
He shall be mercenary, and she shall be foolish.

connotation.why: money-minded, set against prudent or materialistic

examples: The little village fair had turned into a mercenary enterprise.

oewn-01713534-s.learner: fighting for pay in the army of a country that is not your own.
examples: The king hired mercenary soldiers from abroad.
